---
title: "4. Are models consistent across near-identical complexes?"
format:
  html:
    code-fold: true
    toc: true
    embed-resources: true
jupyter: python3
---

The benchmark contains allelic effector series (AVR-PikD/E/A/C/F) and engineered
HMA variants, so many references differ by one or two residues. If accuracy is a
smooth function of the input, near-identical complexes should score alike. A
resurfacing campaign generates variants one or two residues from a known
complex, so a model that flips its answer on such pairs cannot rank designs
regardless of its aggregate accuracy.

A pair counts as near-identical when both chains are at least 95% identical.
Identity is matched residues in a global BLOSUM62 alignment divided by the
length of the shorter sequence. Gaps are not counted as mismatches, so
substitutions and alignment gap positions are reported separately.

```{python}
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "../../bin")
from _analysis_common import *

d = load()
df, near, lookup, combos = d["df"], d["near"], d["lookup"], d["combos"]
sim = d["sim"]

acc_by_pdb = (df.assign(ok=df[RA_COL] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD)
                .groupby("pdb")["ok"].mean().mul(100))
near["acc_a"] = near["pdb_a"].map(acc_by_pdb)
near["acc_b"] = near["pdb_b"].map(acc_by_pdb)
near = near.dropna(subset=["acc_a", "acc_b"])
near["acc_gap"] = (near["acc_a"] - near["acc_b"]).abs()
print(f"{len(near)} near-identical pairs; accuracy gap spans "
      f"{near['acc_gap'].min():.0f} to {near['acc_gap'].max():.0f} points")
print(f"correlation between identity and accuracy agreement: "
      f"{spearman(d['sim']['min_identity'], (d['sim']['pdb_a'].map(acc_by_pdb) - d['sim']['pdb_b'].map(acc_by_pdb)).abs()):+.3f}")
```

## Near-identical pairs with the widest accuracy gaps

```{python}
cols = ["pdb_a", "pdb_b", "receptor_substitutions", "effector_substitutions",
        "receptor_gap_positions", "effector_gap_positions",
        "acc_a", "acc_b", "acc_gap"]
show = near.sort_values("acc_gap", ascending=False)[cols].head(10).copy()
for c in ["acc_a", "acc_b", "acc_gap"]:
    show[c] = show[c].round(0).astype(int)
show.reset_index(drop=True)
```

- The accuracy gap spans the full range even among pairs where both chains are
  at least 95% identical. Small sequence changes do not produce correspondingly
  small accuracy changes, and identity does not predict agreement.
- Several of the widest gaps come from pairs with an identical receptor and a
  single-digit number of effector substitutions.

## The benchmark's own noise floor

```{python}
GAP_TOL = 6
same_seq = near[(near["receptor_substitutions"] == 0) &
                (near["effector_substitutions"] == 0)].copy()
same_seq["total_gaps"] = (same_seq["receptor_gap_positions"] +
                          same_seq["effector_gap_positions"])
for _, r in same_seq.sort_values("total_gaps").iterrows():
    flag = "" if r["total_gaps"] <= GAP_TOL else "   <- verify the gapped region by hand"
    print(f"{r['pdb_a']} vs {r['pdb_b']}: {r['acc_a']:.0f}% vs {r['acc_b']:.0f}% "
          f"(gap {r['acc_gap']:.0f} points; {int(r['receptor_gap_positions'])} receptor "
          f"+ {int(r['effector_gap_positions'])} effector gap positions){flag}")
```

- Zero substitutions alone does not make two references the same complex. A
  global alignment reports a difference as a gap when it falls in a region one
  construct does not model, so an engineered residue in an unmodelled tail is
  invisible. Both pairs above exceed the gap tolerance and were checked by hand,
  with opposite outcomes.
- 5A6W against 6G10 is the usable control. Both are Pikp-1 HMA with AVR-PikD,
  the effector sequences are identical with no substitutions and no gaps, and
  the receptors differ only in construct boundaries plus a two-residue indel.
  The spread between them cannot be attributed to sequence. It sets a floor on
  the benchmark's reproducibility, reflecting construct, crystal form and which
  copy was extracted.
- 5A6W against 6R8K is not valid. 6R8K carries the engineered NK-KE change in a
  C-terminal tail (`...QANK` becomes `...QAKED`) that 5A6W does not model, so
  the alignment scores it as a gap rather than a substitution.

## Does a single model flip on near-identical pairs?

Shown for the no-MSA design setting, unrestrained and reference-restrained, so
the effect of restraints on the confidence and accuracy relationship is visible
in the same axes. Every other combination is in
`supplementary-figures/confidence-vs-pose/`.

```{python}
CASES = [("boltz2", "no_msa"), ("boltz2_constrained", "no_msa")]

# Labels sit left of their marker by default. These are the ones that would
# collide with a neighbour there, so they go to the right instead. Keyed by
# model, since the two panels place their points differently.
LABEL_ON_RIGHT = {
    "boltz2": {"7A8W", "7QZD"},
    "boltz2_constrained": {"6R8M", "7BNT", "5A6W"},
}


def label_points(ax, fig, pts, xcol, ycol, lcol, on_right=frozenset(), size=6.5):
    """Annotate every point, directly beside its own marker.

    No fanning and no leader lines: a label is always level with its point, so
    it can never be mistaken for a neighbour's. Side is left by default and is
    overridden per PDB via on_right where that would collide or run off-axis.
    """
    for _, r in pts.iterrows():
        left = r[lcol] not in on_right
        ax.annotate(r[lcol], (r[xcol], r[ycol]), fontsize=size,
                    xytext=(-6 if left else 6, 0), textcoords="offset points",
                    ha="right" if left else "left", va="center", zorder=5)


def confidence_panels(metric, xlabel, xlim, name, thesis=False, subdir=None):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, sharex=True, figsize=(9.0, 10.6))
    for ax, (cm, cf) in zip(axes, CASES):
        pts = df[(df["model"] == cm) & (df["msa"] == cf)]
        for _, r in near.iterrows():
            a, b = (lookup.get((cm, cf, r["pdb_a"])),
                    lookup.get((cm, cf, r["pdb_b"])))
            if a is None or b is None:
                continue
            flips = ((a[RA_COL] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD)
                     != (b[RA_COL] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD))
            ax.plot([a[metric], b[metric]], [a[RA_COL], b[RA_COL]],
                    color=("#D55E00" if flips else "#CCCCCC"),
                    lw=(1.0 if flips else 0.7), alpha=0.45,
                    zorder=(3 if flips else 1))
        ax.scatter(pts[metric], pts[RA_COL], s=46, color="#0072B2",
                   edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.5, zorder=4)
        ax.axhline(RA_EFF_THRESHOLD, ls="--", color="grey", lw=1)
        ax.axvline(0.8, ls="--", color="grey", lw=1)
        ax.set_yscale("log")
        ax.set_xlim(*xlim)
        ax.set_title(combo_label(cm, cf), fontsize=11)
        ax.set_ylabel("Receptor-aligned effector RMSD (Å, log scale)")
        readable_log(ax.yaxis, RA_TICKS)
        label_points(ax, fig, pts, metric, RA_COL, "pdb",
                     on_right=LABEL_ON_RIGHT.get(cm, frozenset()))
    axes[-1].set_xlabel(xlabel)
    handles = [plt.Line2D([], [], color="#D55E00", lw=1.4),
               plt.Line2D([], [], color="#CCCCCC", lw=1.4)]
    fig.legend(handles,
               ["\u2265 95% identical pair, only one posed correctly",
                "\u2265 95% identical pair, both same outcome"],
               loc="lower center", ncol=2, frameon=True, fontsize=9,
               bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.004))
    fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.035, 1, 1])
    save_fig(fig, name, thesis=thesis, subdir=subdir)
    plt.show()


confidence_panels("iptm", "ipTM", (0.06, 1.0), "iptm_vs_pose_all_combos")
```

Every pair of benchmark complexes, not only the near-identical ones, so the
near-identical pairs can be read against their background. If pairs differing by
a handful of residues diverge as much as arbitrary pairs, the divergence is not
attributable to the sequence difference between them.

```{python}
def all_pairs_divergence(metric, ylabel, name, max_subs, thesis=False, subdir=None):
    """Every pair, split on how many residues actually differ between them.

    Substitution count rather than percent identity, because identity here is
    contaminated by construct boundaries: two structures of the same protein
    modelled to different termini score as low as 93% while differing by zero
    residues. The count is immune to that and is a more concrete claim.
    """
    cm, cf = "boltz2", "no_msa"
    rows = []
    for _, r in sim.iterrows():
        a, b = lookup.get((cm, cf, r["pdb_a"])), lookup.get((cm, cf, r["pdb_b"]))
        if a is None or b is None or pd.isna(a[metric]) or pd.isna(b[metric]):
            continue
        rows.append({"d_ra": abs(a[RA_COL] - b[RA_COL]),
                     "d_metric": abs(a[metric] - b[metric]),
                     "subs": int(r["receptor_substitutions"]
                                 + r["effector_substitutions"])})
    d = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    d["near"] = d["subs"] <= max_subs

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.4, 5.6))
    for flag, col, size, lab in [
            (False, "#BBBBBB", 34, f"> {max_subs} substitutions"),
            (True, "#D55E00", 52, f"\u2264 {max_subs} substitutions")]:
        s = d[d["near"] == flag]
        ax.scatter(s["d_ra"], s["d_metric"], s=size, color=col,
                   alpha=0.8 if flag else 0.55, edgecolor="black",
                   linewidth=0.4, label=f"{lab} (n={len(s)})",
                   zorder=3 if flag else 2)
    ax.set_xlabel("Difference in receptor-aligned effector RMSD (Å)")
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
    ax.legend(frameon=True, fontsize=8.5, ncol=2, title="Pair differs by",
              loc="lower center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.01))
    fig.tight_layout()
    save_fig(fig, name, thesis=thesis, subdir=subdir)
    plt.show()
    return d


allpairs = all_pairs_divergence(
    "iptm", "Difference in ipTM", "pair_divergence_vs_substitutions",
    max_subs=3, thesis=True)
print(allpairs.groupby("near")[["d_ra", "d_metric"]]
        .agg(["median", "max", "size"]).round(2).to_string())
```

- Without an MSA, ipTM tracks correctness. No failure in either panel reaches
  0.8 and the two distributions barely overlap. The same model with an MSA
  interleaves them, which is why both thesis panels show the no-MSA setting.
- Orange lines join near-identical pairs where one member is solved and the
  other is not. They run diagonally rather than vertically, and flipping pairs
  differ far more in ipTM than pairs that do not flip. The model registers that
  it has changed its answer.
- The 0.8 convention still sits in the wrong place, rejecting most of the
  correct unrestrained poses. Ranking by ipTM is informative here, but the
  conventional threshold is not, and 18 targets in one system cannot fit a
  better one.
- Restraints raise confidence across the board without rescuing the AVR-PikC and
  AVR-PikF evasion variants. Only 7QZD moves, and it remains the boundary case
  in both panels.

### The same panels scored by ipSAE (supplementary)

```{python}
confidence_panels("ipsae_min", "ipSAE (min of the two chain directions)",
                  (-0.04, 1.0), "confidence_vs_pose_ipsae_boltz2_no_msa",
                  subdir="confidence-vs-pose")

for cm, cf in CASES:
    s = df[(df["model"] == cm) & (df["msa"] == cf)]
    ok = s[RA_COL] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD
    print(f"{combo_label(cm, cf)}:")
    for col in ["iptm", "ipsae_min"]:
        print(f"    {col:10s} correct {s[ok][col].min():.3f}-{s[ok][col].max():.3f}"
              f"   failed {s[~ok][col].min():.3f}-{s[~ok][col].max():.3f}"
              f"   overlap={'yes' if s[~ok][col].max() >= s[ok][col].min() else 'NO'}")
```

- ipSAE discriminates worse than ipTM here, which is why the thesis figure uses
  ipTM. Unrestrained, ipTM separates the classes without overlap. ipSAE overlaps
  in both settings.
- The cause is its floor. ipSAE collapses to exactly zero once no residue pair
  clears its PAE cutoff, which catches every unrestrained failure and two
  correct poses. A badly placed effector is not scored low, it is not scored at
  all, and neither is a well-placed one the metric distrusts.
- The floor flattens the ranking within the failures. On the ipTM axis the
  AVR-Pia-site failures stay distinguishable and 7QZD moves visibly under
  restraint. On this axis they stack on the spine.
- Restrained, ipSAE overlaps in the other direction. Failures outscore a correct
  pose, so no single threshold works.

## Self-consistency across all models

```{python}
rows = []
for (m, f), g in df.groupby(["model", "msa"]):
    acc = float((g[RA_COL] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD).mean())
    n = fl = 0
    for _, r in near.iterrows():
        A, B = lookup.get((m, f, r["pdb_a"])), lookup.get((m, f, r["pdb_b"]))
        if A is None or B is None:
            continue
        n += 1
        fl += ((A[RA_COL] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD) != (B[RA_COL] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD))
    exp = 2 * acc * (1 - acc) * n
    rows.append({"model": m, "msa": f, "combo": combo_label(m, f),
                 "accuracy": acc, "pairs": n, "flips": int(fl),
                 "expected": exp, "fewer_than_expected": exp - fl})
cons = pd.DataFrame(rows)

blocks = [("no_msa", cons[cons["msa"] == "no_msa"].sort_values("fewer_than_expected", ascending=False)),
          ("msa", cons[cons["msa"] == "msa"].sort_values("fewer_than_expected", ascending=False))]
cx, cvals, ccols, clabs = [], [], [], []
cursor = 0.0
for flag, blk in blocks:
    for _, r in blk.iterrows():
        cx.append(cursor); cvals.append(r["fewer_than_expected"])
        ccols.append(MSA_COLOR if flag == "msa" else NO_MSA_COLOR)
        clabs.append(pretty(r["model"])); cursor += 1
    cursor += 1.2

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 6.2))
ax.bar(cx, cvals, width=0.85, color=ccols, edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.7)
ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=1)
ax.set_xticks(cx)
ax.set_xticklabels(clabs, rotation=45, ha="right", fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylabel("Consistency\n(expected − observed verdict changes)")
msa_legend(ax)
save_fig(fig, "self_consistency")
plt.show()

out = cons[["combo", "accuracy", "pairs", "flips", "expected",
            "fewer_than_expected"]].copy()
out["accuracy"] = (100 * out["accuracy"]).round(0)
out[["expected", "fewer_than_expected"]] = out[["expected", "fewer_than_expected"]].round(1)
out.sort_values("fewer_than_expected", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
```

- A raw flip count would punish mid-accuracy models and flatter any model that
  is uniformly right or uniformly wrong. Each count is therefore compared
  against the number expected if the two members of a pair were unrelated draws
  at that variant's own accuracy. Above zero means more self-consistent than
  accuracy alone predicts.
- AlphaFold3 and Boltz-1 with an MSA are genuinely self-consistent rather than
  merely accurate. Boltz-2 with an MSA sits at its expectation, so knowing it
  solved one member of a near-identical pair says nothing about the other.
- ColabFold without an MSA should be ignored here. It records few flips because
  it solves almost nothing, so its expectation is tiny. That bar reflects
  failure rather than consistency.
- The pairs are drawn from 18 structures and overlap heavily, so the ordering is
  indicative rather than firm.


## Every model, same view (supplementary)

The same view for every variant, written to
`supplementary-figures/confidence-vs-pose/`. Two differences from the panel
above. The axes are shared across all panels, which makes them comparable but
means no panel is scaled to its own data. There is also no broken axis, since
that split is specific to Boltz-2 with an MSA.

```{python}
ra_lo = max(df[RA_COL].min() * 0.8, 0.2)
ra_hi = df[RA_COL].max() * 1.25
n = 0

for flag, model in combos:
    sub = df[(df["model"] == model) & (df["msa"] == flag)]
    if sub.empty or sub["iptm"].isna().all():
        continue
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6, 5.8))

    n_flip = 0
    for _, r in near.iterrows():
        a, b = lookup.get((model, flag, r["pdb_a"])), lookup.get((model, flag, r["pdb_b"]))
        if a is None or b is None:
            continue
        flips = ((a[RA_COL] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD) != (b[RA_COL] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD))
        n_flip += bool(flips)
        ax.plot([a["iptm"], b["iptm"]], [a[RA_COL], b[RA_COL]],
                color=("#D55E00" if flips else "#CCCCCC"),
                lw=(1.0 if flips else 0.7), alpha=0.45,
                zorder=(3 if flips else 1))

    ax.scatter(sub["iptm"], sub[RA_COL], s=44,
               color=(MSA_COLOR if flag == "msa" else NO_MSA_COLOR),
               edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.5, zorder=4)
    for i, (_, r) in enumerate(sub.sort_values("iptm").iterrows()):
        left = r["iptm"] > 0.72
        ax.annotate(r["pdb"], (r["iptm"], r[RA_COL]), fontsize=6.5,
                    xytext=(-6 if left else 6, 3 if i % 2 == 0 else -8),
                    textcoords="offset points",
                    ha="right" if left else "left", va="center", zorder=5)

    ax.axhline(RA_EFF_THRESHOLD, ls="--", color="grey", lw=1)
    ax.axvline(CONF_THRESHOLD, ls="--", color="grey", lw=1)
    ax.set_yscale("log")
    readable_log(ax.yaxis, RA_TICKS)
    ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
    ax.set_ylim(ra_lo, ra_hi)
    ax.set_xlabel("ipTM")
    ax.set_ylabel("Receptor-aligned effector RMSD (Å, log scale)")
    n_ok = int((sub[RA_COL] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD).sum())
    flag_txt = "  [restraints from the reference]" if is_oracle(model) else ""
    ax.set_title(f"{combo_label(model, flag)}  {n_ok}/{len(sub)} correct, "
                 f"{n_flip}/{len(near)} pairs flip{flag_txt}", fontsize=9)
    save_fig(fig, f"confidence_vs_pose_{model}_{flag}", subdir="confidence-vs-pose")
    plt.close(fig)
    n += 1
print(f"wrote {n} panels to supplementary-figures/confidence-vs-pose/")
```

- The two reference-restrained variants are flagged in their panel titles. Their
  points sit low and left, which is what being told the interface looks like.
  They are not comparable to the predictors around them.
- Among genuine predictors, the contrast between a tight low cluster and a
  diagonal smear is the same distinction the flip counts capture numerically
  above.
